title: Incident response and reporting
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and apply: incident response and reporting

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Overview
instruction.body: In this lesson, practise incident response and reporting using an authorised work order and a realistic Australian cleaning-site scenario. Work only within training, employer procedures and site-specific instructions.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: For injury or exposure, stop work, make the area safe, follow emergency instructions, seek first aid or emergency help as appropriate, and record facts promptly.

instruction.heading: Recognise an incident
instruction.body: An incident can include injury, near miss, spill, property damage or an unsafe condition. Distinguish immediate danger from an issue that can be safely isolated and reported.

instruction.heading: Respond in priority order
instruction.body: Stop the affected task, protect yourself and others, and contact emergency services for an emergency using local site procedures. Do not attempt rescue, chemical neutralisation or first aid beyond training.

instruction.heading: Report facts and follow up
instruction.body: Record what happened, where and when, who was notified and any immediate controls. Avoid speculation or assigning blame. Preserve evidence according to employer policy and confirm handover.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Recognise the event as an incident, which can include an injury, near miss, spill, property damage or unsafe condition.
Distinguish immediate danger from a problem that can be safely isolated and reported.
Stop the affected task and make the area safe before anything else.
Protect yourself and others, and contact emergency services for an emergency using the local site procedure.
For an injury or exposure, follow emergency instructions and seek first aid, without attempting rescue, chemical neutralisation or first aid beyond your training.
Record what happened, where and when, who was notified and any immediate controls, without speculation or blame.
Preserve evidence according to employer policy and confirm the handover.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: The affected task is stopped and the area is made safe before anything else.
Emergency services are contacted for an emergency using the local site procedure.
No rescue, chemical neutralisation or first aid is attempted beyond training.
The report records what happened, where and when, who was notified and the controls applied, with no speculation or blame.
summary: For an injury or exposure, the cleaner stops work, makes the area safe, follows emergency instructions and records the facts promptly.
Incidents include injuries, near misses, spills, property damage and unsafe conditions, and immediate danger is kept separate from issues that can be isolated and reported.
The report sets out what happened, where and when, who was notified and the immediate controls, with no speculation or blame.

knowledgeChecks.question: Should a near miss be reported even if nobody is hurt?
options: No, only injuries need reporting and only the bigger ones count
Only if the supervisor asks for it later and only when someone is hurt
Yes. A near miss counts as an incident, so record the facts promptly
Only if the damage costs more than a set amount and not before the shift ends

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the first response to an incident when no instruction has been given?
options: Continue and report it at the end of the shift and keep working in the same area
Ask the client what they would like you to do and wait for their reply in the room
Stop the affected task and protect yourself and others until the instruction is given
Attempt rescue or chemical neutralisation yourself before anyone else arrives on site

knowledgeChecks.question: Which of these does the lesson list as an incident?
